newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ILP sees pretax loss for first half of year.
newsitem.headline: ILP sees pretax loss for first half of year.

text.p: Irish packaging company ILP Plc said on Wednesday that it had seen no recovery in demand in the second quarter after a disappointing first quarter and expected to post a pretax loss for the first six months of 1997.
But it said the group had significantly scaled back its expense base in keeping with the current situation and expected a profitable outcome for the year as a whole.

Chairman John Bourke said in a statement that customers continued to expect a stronger market in the second half of 1997 and its new Leixlip plant is now fully commissioned which will enable it to keep pace with any increase in demand.

Bourke recalled that he told the annual meeting on May 1 that first quarter demand had been disappointing and said that since then a number of major electronic producers had commented on first half weakness in their markets, especially in Europe.

"ILP in turn, whilst experiencesing some increase in demand in April, have seen no recovery in demand overall in the second quarter. Accordingly we estimate a loss before tax for the first six months this year," Bourke said.
